title: Case #002
question: Whose story is the evidence telling?

suspects.label: The Sopranos
suspects.whyPlausible: The answer. Every exhibit is a wall of the same house: the club, the office, the ducks, the diner, the credits, the pines, the black screen.

suspects.label: Goodfellas
suspects.whyPlausible: The neon club and the diner booth read as Scorsese; the marquee mob suspect most players reach for.

suspects.label: The Godfather
suspects.whyPlausible: The default answer to anything mob-shaped.

suspects.label: Casino
suspects.whyPlausible: Neon nightlife after midnight reads Vegas as easily as Jersey.

suspects.label: Analyze This
suspects.whyPlausible: Literally a mob boss in therapy, from 1999. The intended wrong theory — the office exhibit fits it perfectly.

suspects.label: Donnie Brasco
suspects.whyPlausible: Undercover mob drama of the same era; clubs and diners fit.

suspects.label: Boardwalk Empire
suspects.whyPlausible: The other famous New Jersey crime series with famous opening credits — survives almost everything.

suspects.label: Jersey Boys
suspects.whyPlausible: A New Jersey music story with mob edges — the neon club and the jukebox diner fit it surprisingly well.

suspects.label: The Wire
suspects.whyPlausible: Prestige crime television of the same rank and era.

suspects.label: Mad Men
suspects.whyPlausible: Prestige television with lounges, offices and a famous title sequence — survives the credits exhibit that kills every film.

authorNotes.meaning: A neon Jersey club at night — Silvio's territory. Deliberately ambiguous: it fits half the board. It quietly rules out period pieces like The Godfather; a 1990s strip-mall club belongs to no 1940s New York.

Two chairs facing each other: someone in this story is in therapy. That sentence has no place in Goodfellas, Casino, Donnie Brasco, Jersey Boys or The Wire — but it fits Analyze This perfectly, which is the trap. The chair belongs to Dr. Melfi, played by Lorraine Bracco, who turned down the mob-wife archetype to sit on the other side of the room.

Ducks at a backyard pool. In the pilot, the ducks trigger the panic attacks that send the protagonist into that office. Analyze This has the mob boss and the therapist — but it has no ducks and no pool. This is the exhibit that breaks the intended wrong theory.

evidence.caption: The onion rings are the best in the state.

authorNotes.meaning: The finale scene with the people removed: red booths, onion rings, a tabletop jukebox. Fans feel it immediately. As elimination work, Baltimore's The Wire has no claim to this booth.

The most famous opening credits in television are a drive: out of the tunnel, through the toll, down the Turnpike, home to the driveway. This exhibit kills every film on the board in one stroke — movies aren't remembered for credits you watch eighty-six times. Only the television suspects survive.

evidence.caption: They were only supposed to be gone an hour.

authorNotes.meaning: Snowy pines and one set of footprints: the 'Pine Barrens' episode, two men lost overnight in the South Jersey woods. Nothing in Mad Men's Manhattan puts it here. After this exhibit, two suspects remain — both New Jersey, both television.

The smoking gun: the most argued-about ten seconds in television history, when the screen simply cut to black. The date settles the last stand-off — Boardwalk Empire didn't premiere until 2010. Only one story ends here.

investigationPaths.name: The New Jersey route
investigationPaths.startingPoint: The club, the credits, the pines

investigationPaths.name: The ending route
investigationPaths.startingPoint: The diner and the black screen

hints.text: The club, the two chairs and the ducks all belong to one man's week.
Ask which suspects could be famous for their opening credits. That single question clears most of the board.
Two suspects share a state. Only one of them ends mid-song.

reveal.summary: The Sopranos. A New Jersey club run by a consigliere. A therapist's office where a Goodfellas wife chose the other chair. Ducks in a backyard pool that sent a mob boss into panic attacks — the same year Hollywood played the idea for laughs in Analyze This. Opening credits that were just a drive down the Turnpike. Two men lost in the snowy Pine Barrens. And a family in a diner booth, onion rings on the table, Journey on the jukebox — until the screen cut to black on June 10, 2007.
reveal.evidenceToAnswer: Each exhibit is one wall of the same house: the club is Silvio's, the office is Melfi's, the ducks are Tony's, the diner is the family's, the credits are the commute, the pines are the show's most famous hour, and the black screen is how it all ended. The office kills the films with no therapy in them; the ducks kill Analyze This; the credits kill the rest of the movies; the pines kill Manhattan; the date kills Boardwalk Empire. Only one suspect survives all seven.
majorConnections: Steve Van Zandt (E Street Band) → Silvio Dante, his first acting role, owner of that club
Lorraine Bracco → from Goodfellas mob wife to Dr. Melfi's chair
Analyze This (1999) → the same-year mob-boss-in-therapy comedy, the board's designed trap
Journey → 'Don't Stop Believin'' on the diner jukebox in the final scene
The New Jersey Turnpike → the opening-credits drive
alternatePaths: Therapy first: the office plus the ducks break the comedy trap early
New Jersey first: the club, the credits and the pines triangulate the state and the medium
The ending first: the diner and the black screen are enough for anyone who lived through 2007
reveal.ohMoment: The moment the player realizes the evidence isn't pointing at a movie — it's pointing at a life. A club, a therapist, ducks in a pool, a commute, a diner. And then the screen goes black, mid-song, and they remember the argument everyone had the next morning: 'Wait — is that IT?'

entryPoints.description: The club and diner read as Scorsese; Analyze This carries film fans deep into the case before the ducks and credits turn them around.
The opening-credits exhibit and the cut to black are shared television memory — even non-viewers know the ending was an event.
The Turnpike drive and the Pine Barrens are solvable from general knowledge of New Jersey, no episodes required.

editorial.notes: SUSPECT FUNNEL: exhibit I fits nearly the whole board; the office builds the Analyze This trap while quietly killing the no-therapy films; the ducks break the trap; the credits cull every remaining film in one stroke; the pines kill Manhattan; the black screen's date is the smoking gun that settles Sopranos vs Boardwalk Empire. Exactly one CONCLUSIVE exhibit, kept last. Media: images are original AI-generated scene evocations; the audio is an original synthesized recording (no copyrighted show material).
